message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No Speed Limit” signs are common on rural interstates; drivers must drive at a safe speed.
• Speed limits are enforced by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) and local law‑enforcement agencies. | Texas DPS – *Speed Limits* page | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | Texas DPS – *Seat Belt Law* | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02% is an offense).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | Texas DPS – *DUI/DWI* | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations can lead to a $50 fine and points on your license. | Texas DPS – *Cell Phone Use* | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs and yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right‑of‑way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas DPS – *Right‑of‑Way* | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas DPS – *Lane Discipline* | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended.
• Cannot pass a stopped school bus until the lights are off and the sign is retracted. | Texas DPS – *School Bus Rules* | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, in front of driveways, or in no‑parking zones.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Texas DPS – *Parking Rules* | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered annually and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass a safety inspection (except for certain exempt categories). | Texas DPS – *Vehicle Registration* | | **Driving Under the Influence of Drugs** | • THC and other drugs are illegal; penalties similar to DUI. | Texas DPS – *Drug‑Related Offenses* | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergency Services** | • 911 for emergencies.
• Texas DPS offers roadside assistance for registered vehicles. | Texas DPS – *Roadside Assistance* | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – The official source for all traffic laws, penalties, and updates. - Website: https://www.dps.texas.gov/ - *Traffic Laws* section: https://www.dps.texas.gov/traffic-laws 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all transportation matters. - Online: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TN/htm/TN.HTM 3. **Local County or City Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional traffic regulations. Check city websites or local law‑enforcement portals. 4. **Texas Highway Patrol** – For specific enforcement questions or clarifications. - Phone: 1‑800‑555‑1234 (example) --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re there for safety. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or listen to music. - **Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection stickers up to date** to avoid fines. - **Be mindful of school buses** – they’re a high‑priority hazard. - **Check for local ordinances** – some areas have unique rules (e.g., no‑stop zones, speed bumps). --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular law (e.g., “What are the penalties for texting while driving?”) or want to know how a recent law change affects you, let me know! I can pull up the exact statute or provide a summary of the latest updates.
